name: Yaben (Konda)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog kond1303 lists no descriptive references; only wordlist-level material (Rosetta Swadesh list) found

sources.citation: Mayor, Infak Insaswar & Yusuf Willem Sawaki. 2025. Exploring alienable-inalienable possessions in Yaben. Linguistik Indonesia 43(2): 205-223. doi:10.26499/li.v43i2.798
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Possession only; the phrase 'stress and intonation patterns' (p.208) is a generic sentence about descriptive method, not Yaben data. Establishes Yaben = Konda [knd], 61% lexical similarity with Yahadian, fieldwork in Konda village 2019.

sources.citation: Holton, Gary & Marian Klamer. 2018. The Papuan languages of East Nusantara and the Bird's Head. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area, 569-640. De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Silent on Konda: Konda appears only in the language table (source Smits & Voorhoeve 1998) and in morphosyntax remarks (no person/gender marking); the stress paragraph (p.587) names other languages.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. 2010. Konda Swadesh List (compiled, sources unnamed).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement; a merged wordlist with sporadic acute accents on two items only (rembitótoy 'straight', bigóbo 'thorn'). Unusable for a rule.

sources.citation: Katubi. 2009. Pilihan bahasa orang Yaben di Papua Barat: tinjauan dari hierarki kebutuhan Maslow. Jurnal Masyarakat dan Budaya 11(1): 83-104. doi:10.14203/jmb.v11i1.236
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Sociolinguistic (language choice/shift); no tekanan, aksen, fonologi, intonasi. Cites the PMB-LIPI 2008 ethnolinguistic fieldwork and Katubi (ed.) 2008.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2004. A short grammar of Inanwatan. Pacific Linguistics 560. Appendix 3 sec. 3 'The Yahadian language', pp. 143-150.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on Konda (mentioned only as a dialect/sister of Yahadian, p.143 fn.). The Yahadian (Mugim) word list carries stress ticks but no prose rule; nothing for Konda.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2002. An introduction to the Inanwatan language of Irian Jaya. In K. A. Adelaar & R. Blust (eds), Between worlds: linguistic papers in memory of David John Prentice, 77-96. Pacific Linguistics 529.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on Konda. Stress statements concern Inanwatan only ('Word stress is unpredictable and distinctive'). Fn. 13: Konda (villages Konda, Sisir) and Yahadian 'seem to be dialects of the Konda-Yahadian language'; Yahadian inventory only.

sources.citation: Berry, Keith & Christine Berry. 1987. A survey of the South Bird's Head Stock. Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 4: 81-117. Abepura: Cenderawasih University & SIL. (Konda sec. 4.1.1 p.92; phonological features sec. 3.3 p.89; Konda word list, K. Berry, Konda village 28.2.86, Appendix C)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. The only phonology (sec. 3.3, p.89) is phonotactic: languages of the stock 'generally do not allow word final consonants and there are very few consonant clusters.. a simple VCV or CVCV syllabic structure'; 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in the article; the Konda list carries no stress marks in the text layer.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 345-459. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey chapter covering the South Bird's Head super-stock incl. Konda-Yahadian; sometimes gives family-level phonological notes (stress) from Cowan/Anceaux data. Open PDF exists but sealang.net was unreachable and ANU DSpace search returned nothing at download time.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Entry 57 KONDA p.34; 40-item list no. 57 (Anceaux data).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Classification, village, sources (Cowan 1953 (GN), 1958a, 1960, 1963, 1965b) and an unmarked 40-word list; shows Cowan 1953 is the only 'grammatical notes' source ever listed for Konda.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page kond1303; Wikipedia 'Konda language (Papuan)' (wikitext)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog's one descriptive reference is Mayor 2019 (UNIPA MA thesis). Wikipedia has no phonology section and says Konda 'is poorly documented'. PHOIBLE's link from kond1303 ('EA 2481', Krishnamurti & Benham 1998) is the Dravidian Konda inventory mis-mapped, not this language.
Phonology section empty ('..'); sources listed are Voorhoeve 1975:34, Berry & Berry 1987:92,98, de Vries 2004:143. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Mayor, Infak Insaswar. 2019. Possessive construction in Yaben. MA thesis, Universitas Negeri Papua (UNIPA), Manokwari. xviii+57 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only descriptive work Glottolog lists for kond1303, based on 2019 fieldwork in Konda village; an MA thesis of this length normally opens with an orthography/phonology sketch that may state stress placement.

sources.citation: Katubi (ed.). 2008. Ekologi Bahasa Yaben: Diferensiasi Intraetnik (N. Kleden-Probonegoro, Katubi, F. H. Tondo, Imelda). Jakarta: LIPI Press. vii+116 pp. ISBN 978-979-799-342-9.

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: PMB-LIPI ethnolinguistic monograph on Yaben with sec. 3.5 'Perbedaan Leksikal dan Fonologis dalam Bahasa Yaben' (pp. 48-52: vowel and consonant differences between Yaben-Konda and Yaben-Simora/Wamargege). Google full-text index has no hits for tekanan/aksen/intonasi, so a stress statement is unlikely but it is the only Indonesian phonological description of the language.

sources.citation: Smits, Leo & C. L. Voorhoeve (eds.). 1998. The J. C. Anceaux collection of wordlists of Irian Jaya languages B: Non-Austronesian (Papuan) languages, Part II. Irian Jaya Source Materials 10. Leiden/Jakarta: DSALCUL/IRIS.

sources.note: Fuller Anceaux Konda wordlist (the source Holton & Klamer 2018 cite for Konda); Anceaux's transcriptions often mark stress, which would give stress-marked data even without a prose rule.
